minor.issue: When JWT auth fails, backend calls ws.close(code=4401) before accept(). The Kubernetes/ingress proxy converts this into an HTTP 403 upgrade rejection at handshake — clients never observe the 4401 code directly (they see an InvalidStatus 403). Behaviour is still 'connection refused' as specified, but if a native client relies on parsing 4401 specifically, it will need to treat 403 as equivalent. Consider ws.accept()+ws.close(4401) so clients get the WS close frame.

integration_issues.flow: Admin dashboard WS on first page load
integration_issues.issue: React StrictMode double-mount causes the initial WebSocket to close (code 1006) immediately ("WebSocket is closed before the connection is established") and reconnect. If a business event fires in this ~1-2s reconnect gap, the client misses it (no count-up, no audit entry). Reproduced once in the first UI test run: receita stayed at 60 € after a redemption; a subsequent reload run showed the correct 80€ -> 82€. Recommend: skip StrictMode for the WS effect, or wait for ws.readyState===OPEN before firing 'ligado' callback (services/ws.js already only sets state on open, but the effect cleanup closes the first socket).

action_items: (Optional/minor) In backend/realtime.py, consider ws.accept() before ws.close(code=4401) so downstream clients receive a 4401 close frame instead of the proxy-substituted HTTP 403 upgrade rejection.

(Optional/minor) Protect against React StrictMode double-mount closing the very first WS: either guard the useEffect with a mount-once ref, or buffer emit() misses server-side by re-broadcasting recent audit entries on ws connect.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/realtime.py: single-process, in-memory _clients set — fine for --workers 1 but will silently drop events if the server is ever scaled to multiple workers or replicas. Add a note or migrate to a pub/sub (Redis) before horizontal scaling.
backend/realtime.py: emit() swallows exceptions when no running loop is present (fine for tests) but does not log; consider a debug log so missed emits are traceable.

frontend/src/pages/AdminDashboard.jsx: split_executado handler adds `v * 0.10` to comissoes even though `v` is already the commission (valor_plataforma). This double-counts commission on-screen (10% of 2€ = 0.2€ added instead of 2€). Confirmed live: receita 80→82 (+2 ✓), but comissoes 8→10 (+2, not +0.2). Wait, on-screen it shows comissoes went 8€→10€ which matches +2€ not +0.2 — but the CODE says v*0.10 = 0.2. Suspected discrepancy: number rounding via eur(Math.round(v)) hides the true increment, or the stat mutates twice. Recommend logging real committed value and fixing to `+ v` (parity with receita) since valor_plataforma is already the platform commission.
frontend/src/services/ws.js: cleanup closes the socket unconditionally on unmount; in React StrictMode dev this causes an immediate close-then-reopen that can drop events emitted in the gap.

backend/routes_admin.py: create_item emits cupons_gerados only for kind=campanhas — good, but response includes `parceiro`/`influencer` label strings that may be stale if resolve_campaign() didn't find them; not a bug for this test.

rca of the issue: No production bug uncovered. Two soft issues surfaced: (1) proxy strips WS 4401 close code because backend closes before accept — cosmetic, still refuses connection as specified; (2) React StrictMode causes first-mount WS to disconnect+reconnect, so business events emitted in that ~1s window are missed on very first page load — recommend either mount-once guard or server-side replay of last N audit entries on connect.
